title: IFR Equipment: GRABCARD + the Checks
hook: Is this airplane even legal for IFR? Grab a card.

scenes.narration: New-to-you rental, and tomorrow's trip is I F R. The panel looks complete... but 'looks complete' isn't a maintenance record, kid. Two questions: what must be INSTALLED, and what must be CHECKED.
Before the list — the altimeter-static and transponder inspections. How many calendar months are they good for? Commit to a number.

Twenty-four calendar months, both of them. Why both? A leaking static system lies to the altimeter AND the transponder at the same time — then everyone on frequency sees the wrong altitude. They expire quietly, kid. Check the logbooks, not the vibes.

Now the installed list — GRAB CARD, on top of day and night V F R gear: Generator or alternator. Radios for the route. Altimeter, the sensitive kind. Ball. Clock with seconds. Attitude indicator. Rate of turn. Directional gyro.
Eyes off the screen. All eight letters, with their words. My coffee and I will wait.
GRAB CARD for the panel. Twenty-four months for the plumbing. An airplane that can't prove it, can't file it.
onScreenText: Can't prove it → can't file it

scenes.narration: From the V O R check lesson — the four tolerances, in order. Four, four... you finish it.
Ninety-one two-oh-five paragraph d. Bring the logbooks and a flashlight.

quiz.question: The altimeter/static system (91.411) and transponder (91.413) checks are required every:
quiz.explanation: Both inspections run on a 24-calendar-month clock — and IFR flight requires the 91.411 check to be current.

quiz.question: In GRABCARD, the second A stands for:
quiz.explanation: G-R-A-B-C-A-R-D: Generator, Radios, Altimeter, Ball, Clock, Attitude indicator, Rate of turn, Directional gyro. (91.205(d))

quiz.question: The clock required for IFR must display:
choices: Hours, minutes, seconds — sweep hand or digital
quiz.explanation: 91.205(d) requires a clock showing hours, minutes, and seconds with a sweep-second pointer or digital presentation.
